Lightning strikes cause significant damage to polymeric composite aircraft structures due to their poor electrical conductivity.
Lightning strike damage includes mechanical cracking, delamination, pyrolytic decomposition, and potential ignition of composite materials.
Traditional LSP solutions include metallic meshes, metallized fibers, conductive paints, and carbon nanostructures.
The novel composite uses polyaniline (PANI), an intrinsically conductive polymer, as a conductive filler.
Carbon fiber reinforcement is integrated to provide mechanical strength and enhance electrical conductivity.
The ICP-based composite avoids metallic inserts to reduce weight and corrosion risks.
Percolation theory guided the determination of the optimal ICP content for conductivity and mechanical balance.
SAE ARP 5412A and 5414A define lightning zones and current waveforms for aircraft LSP design.
Lightning currents can reach up to 200 kA in critical zones like nose and wing tips.
Most of the fuselage experiences lightning currents up to 2 kA, with common strikes between 5-10 kA.
Metallized meshes complicate manufacturing and increase aircraft weight.
Metallized paints are generally ineffective for high current discharges due to low thickness and particle content.
Carbon nanotube composites have excellent LSP properties but are cost-prohibitive for industrial use.
The ICP-based composite exhibits electrical and thermal conductivity comparable to metallized fiber composites.
Manufacturing the ICP composite is simpler and lower cost compared to metallic mesh solutions.
Aircraft grounding for lightning strike repairs can take up to 6 working days, increasing operational costs.
The developed composite meets key aerospace LSP standards and regulations.
The composite surfacing films and embedded metallic foils are common in current LSP solutions but add weight.
The ICP composite aims to maintain a good strength-to-mass ratio while providing effective LSP.
Further research is needed to optimize the ICP composite's physical and processing properties.
